scope: Isolated numeric-transport restore race prototype, not an integrated fix
diagnostic: A previously selected numeric candidate is mutated while the next asynchronous lookup runs. Before the prototype, the restored first array contains the changed value rather than the saved value.
prototype: Keep staging bytes for reused candidates until all asynchronous reconstruction completes, then revalidate without yielding and replace changed candidates before assembling the graph.

validation.before: Race regression failed: expected 1, received 999; 16 other transport tests passed.
validation.after: 54 transport, numeric reuse, encoding-client and decoding-client tests passed, including graph alias preservation, unchanged second candidate reuse and protection of shared or graph-aliased staging buffers.
validation.viteBuild: Direct Vite build passed after preparing the CAD kernel; a complete production build was not run.
validation.typecheck: All 15 batches passed on a 360-second guarded retry before two additional backing-buffer tests were added. The first 180-second lease expired at batch 11 with cleanup confirmed and no reported TypeScript error.
validation.mcpBrowserSmoke: Passed the small GUI/public-MCP project import and reopen smoke at a 1664995328-byte Job peak. The initial attempt failed because the direct Vite build lacked the CAD kernel; preparing the kernel and rebuilding resolved that setup failure. This does not reproduce the race.
validation.realPly3: Not run: observed free disk was approximately 3.80 GB, below the established 4.00 GB initial admission guard. The guard was not lowered.

representativeTransformControl.scope: Shared-operation diagnostic on the integration branch, not GUI or public MCP concurrency
representativeTransformControl.result: During a cooperative numeric reuse lookup, Scale, Flip Normals and Mirror each returned independent output and left the 65538-value source unchanged. The unpacked graph reused the original matching source.
representativeTransformControl.typecheck: Focused test and imported source passed; an earlier external temporary config could not resolve vite/client and was replaced with a config under the checkout.
representativeTransformControl.limitation: This manufactured interleaving does not establish immutability for every operation or demonstrate that normal GUI or MCP actions can trigger the low-level mutation race.

browserWorkerRaceDiagnostic.scope: Real browser decoding worker with an injected mutation in the reuse callback; not a normal GUI or MCP trigger
browserWorkerRaceDiagnostic.method: Two 73728-value mesh arrays are encoded, registered as reusable candidates and decoded by the browser worker. The diagnostic mutates the first source during the second reuse lookup and verifies the first decoded value.
browserWorkerRaceDiagnostic.baseline: Failed: the restored first candidate contained the injected mutation.
browserWorkerRaceDiagnostic.prototype: Passed the same interleaving, checked decoded aliases and display cache, and confirmed normal and cancelled decoder worker termination. Peak Job memory was 890982400 bytes.
browserWorkerRaceDiagnostic.limitation: The prototype still does not address mutation after unpack returns, and the large-resource gate remains untested.

stagingLifetimeDiagnostic.scope: Synthetic Node transport run using the four Float64 staging sizes observed in PLY-3; not a real browser or end-to-end resource result
stagingLifetimeDiagnostic.interpretation: The prototype retains about 439 MB more ArrayBuffer storage at the fourth lookup. Both runs start with all staging buffers allocated, so the comparison does not by itself determine the real Job peak or prove failure.

fingerprintExperiment.scope: Separate low-level Node experiment; not wired to the application
fingerprintExperiment.method: Hash validated staging bytes, release them as before, then synchronously fingerprint each reused array and reject if it changed. This fails closed but does not retry the restore.
fingerprintExperiment.smallTests: Two passed: changed first candidate rejected and unchanged signed-zero alias retained.
fingerprintExperiment.sizedDiagnostic: At PLY-3 staging sizes, ArrayBuffer measurements at the four lookups were 460495699, 194387723, 149491595 and 21562427 bytes. The test run took about 5.47 seconds versus about 0.85 seconds for the current transport control. The first run exceeded the default 5-second test timeout; an explicit 30-second retry completed.
fingerprintExperiment.limitations: The synchronous hash is a potential long main-thread task; timings are Node synthetic measurements, not browser responsiveness. There is no retry, no protection after unpack returns, and no GUI/MCP or real PLY-3 validation. It is not an integrated solution.

limitations: The reproducer uses a low-level callback; a normal GUI or MCP mutation has not been demonstrated.
The prototype keeps staging buffers alive longer, so it may exceed the 4 GiB resource budget on the real workload.

GUI open and MCP import can perform asynchronous CAD restoration after decoding, before publication. A separate low-level diagnostic mutated the reused source after unpack returned and observed the changed value in the decoded result; it does not establish that normal GUI or MCP actions mutate the array.
